# Copilot instructions for `chatbot`

## Build and test commands

This repository is a Common Lisp ASDF system named `chatbot`. Quicklisp and SBCL are assumed.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Load the system | `sbcl --non-interactive --eval '(require :asdf)' --eval '(asdf:load-system :chatbot)'` |
| Load the test system | `sbcl --non-interactive --eval '(require :asdf)' --eval '(asdf:load-system "chatbot/tests")'` |
| Run the full test suite | `sbcl --non-interactive --eval '(require :asdf)' --eval '(asdf:test-system :chatbot)'` |
| Run the full test suite via wrapper script | `sbcl --non-interactive --load run-tests.lisp` |
| Run one test | `sbcl --non-interactive --eval '(require :asdf)' --eval '(asdf:load-system "chatbot/tests")' --eval '(fiveam:run (quote chatbot::test-default-conversation))'` |

Single tests are FiveAM test symbols loaded by the `chatbot/tests` ASDF system; replace `chatbot::test-default-conversation` with the specific test name you need. `chatbot/tests`' `test-op` calls `chatbot::run-all-tests`, so a green ASDF test-system run and a green `run-all-tests` are equivalent. Test files live under `tests/` (one file per subsystem slice: `tests-payloads`, `tests-runtime`, `tests-round-robin`, `tests-sandbox`, `tests-openai`, `tests-google`, `tests-personas`, `tests-mcp`, `tests-agentic-loops`, `tests-chromadb`); some of these files are very large (100+ KB), see `TECHNICAL_DEBT.md` before adding much more to them.

## High-level architecture

- `chatbot.asd` defines two systems: runtime code lives in `chatbot` (under `src/`, organized into `core/`, `utils/`, `mcp/`, `attachments/`, `prompts/`, `payloads/`, `personas/`, `backends/`, `orchestration/`, `tools/`), and FiveAM tests live in `chatbot/tests` (under `tests/`). Keep runtime files out of the test system, keep test files out of the runtime system, and declare explicit `:depends-on` edges for new files in `chatbot.asd`.
- **Data model (`src/core/data.lisp`)**: `chatbot` and `conversation` are composition roots built from small single-concern component classes rather than flat "god objects" — `chatbot` is composed of `chatbot-identity`, `chatbot-llm-config`, `chatbot-prompt-config`, `chatbot-cache-config`, `chatbot-tool-config`, `chatbot-mcp-state`, `chatbot-minion-state`, plus an optional `runtime-context`; `conversation` is composed of a `history` (messages/persona memory/diary/prompt decorations, backed by a persistent linked `history-node` chain), `cache-state`, `swp-state` (the "Sticky Warmth Protocol" Flash/Pro failover state machine), and `metrics`. Backwards-compatible forwarding accessors (e.g. `chatbot-model`, `conversation-messages`) delegate to the underlying component slots, so treat those accessors as the stable API even though the storage is nested.
- **Runtime context (`src/core/data.lisp`, `src/core/vars.lisp`)**: a `runtime-context` object (not a bare global) carries per-run configuration and shared services — HTTP verb functions, API-key lookup, logging config/level/stream, timeouts, the MCP config path override, the shared `startup-chatbot`, the agentic-loop registry, the unified worker registry, and thread-local active-conversation/active-planner state. There is no ambient `*default-conversation*`/`*startup-chatbot*` global anymore; `src/core/vars.lisp`'s `define-runtime-context-accessor` macro generates `current-*` accessor pairs (e.g. `current-default-conversation`, `current-startup-chatbot`, `current-active-conversation`) that read/write through `(resolve-runtime-context context)`, defaulting to `*active-runtime-context*` / `*default-runtime-context*` when no context is passed explicitly.
- **Chat entry/dispatch chain**: `chat` (`src/core/chat.lisp`) → resolves a `runtime-context` via `resolve-chat-entry-context` (`src/core/chat-entry.lisp`) → `execute-chat-entry-shell` binds the active conversation/context for the duration of the call → `chat-turn` resolves the target conversation (`resolve-chat-conversation`/`route-chat-turn-conversation` in `src/core/chat-routing.lisp`, which reroutes input to an active planner minion when Planning Mode is engaged) → prepares per-turn state (file attachments, effective model/generation-config, a cloned conversation) → `dispatch-chat-turn` looks up the backend handler in the **pluggable backend registry** (`src/core/backend-registry.lisp`: `*chat-backends*` hash table, populated by each backend file calling `register-chat-backend` at load time, e.g. `backend-gemini.lisp` registers `:gemini`, `backend-openai.lisp` registers `:openai`/`:lm-studio`/`:grok`, `backend-google.lisp` registers `:google`) and invokes it.
- Backend state is intentionally different by provider:
  - Gemini Interactions uses `conversation-interaction-id` for multi-turn state and streams SSE events; it also supports Google's explicit `cachedContents` caching (`src/backends/google-caching.lisp`: fingerprinting, TTL, create/reuse/refresh policy).
  - OpenAI, LM Studio, and Grok rebuild history from `conversation-messages` every turn and stream chat-completions deltas.
  - Google `generateContent` is non-streaming and also relies on explicit `conversation-messages`.
  - All three backends share `src/backends/turn-runner.lisp`, which normalizes provider outcomes into `:final` / `:tools` / `:retry` and drives the shared recursion/tool-execution/error-handling loop (`run-provider-turn-loop`), so provider files only need to build/parse provider-specific payloads.
- Gemini's legacy 404 fallback to Google `generateContent` is an explicit compatibility flag on the chatbot (`:gemini-fallback-to-google-p`, default `nil`) rather than an unconditional silent switch.
- **Tool calling is recursive in all backends**: the model response is parsed for tool requests, `execute-chatbot-tool` (`src/mcp/tool-execution.lisp`) dispatches to either a built-in tool or a remote MCP tool, the result is converted back into the provider-specific message shape, and the backend calls itself again to continue the turn. Built-in tools are a local registry (`builtin-dispatch.lisp` + `define-builtin-tool`, with actual name→handler bindings in `builtin-registrations.lisp`, and implementations split by domain: `filesystem-tools.lisp`, `chatbot-state-tools.lisp`, `eval-grounding-tools.lisp`, `git-tools.lisp`, `shell-tools.lisp`, `planner-minion-tools.lisp`, `mcp/agentic-loop-tools.lisp`); MCP tools are remote JSON-RPC tools discovered from connected servers (`mcp-dispatch.lisp`, `tool-registry.lisp` merges/normalizes both sources). Post-execution side effects (e.g. ChromaDB knowledge-graph sync) run through a registered hook framework (`*tool-after-execution-hooks*`) rather than being hardcoded into the dispatcher.
- `src/mcp/mcp.lisp` owns the MCP client core (JSON-RPC requests, reader loop, `tools/list` caching/invalidation). `mcp-lifecycle.lisp` launches/stops MCP subprocesses (tracked by the runtime context's `resource-supervisor` for guaranteed cleanup), `mcp-config.lisp` parses the s-expression (not JSON) MCP config file, and `mcp-startup.lisp` wires the shared startup servers onto a runtime context. `initialize-startup-chatbot` is idempotent — repeated calls reuse the shared startup chatbot instead of relaunching MCP servers, and `new-chat` reuses that shared server list when one already exists.
- **Orchestration (`src/orchestration/`)**: an *agentic loop* is an autonomous worker thread that repeatedly runs chat/tool steps toward a goal, with approval pause/resume and watchdog-driven restarts; it's split across `agentic-loop-startup.lisp` (clone/strip conversation, inject loop system instructions, resolve backend/model), `agentic-loop-state.lisp` (the `agentic-loop` object + per-context registry), `agentic-loop-worker.lisp` (the run loop, approvals, failures, restarts), and `agentic-loop-monitor.lisp` (a global watchdog thread reaping zombies/orphans). `round-robin-chat` (`round-robin.lisp`) feeds one input through a configured list of participants in order, cloning each participant's conversation and building a shared transcript; `run-arena` makes personas debate each other's outputs over multiple rounds. `sandbox-personas.lisp` implements a name-keyed persona registry (`spawn-persona`, `list-personas`, `remove-persona`) for multi-agent/background tasking outside the single default conversation.
- **Persistence**: conversations/minions can be checkpointed to JSON and restored (`src/core/conversation-persistence.lisp`, schema defined in `src/core/checkpoint-schema.lisp`); `src/core/conversation-compression.lisp` trims/compresses history into synthetic digest messages as context grows; `src/core/conversation-constructors.lisp` builds fresh `chatbot`/`conversation` instances from persona/config input (used by both `new-chat` and checkpoint restore).
- Persona preload is implemented as synthetic conversation history, not a separate memory store. `new-chat-persona` loads `config.lisp`, `system-instruction.md` / `system-instructions.md`, optional `compressed-memory.txt` or `memory.json`, and any sorted diary files from `CompressedDiary/` when present or `Diary/` otherwise, then seeds the conversation with synthetic preload history before the first live turn. When `memory.json` is present, persona startup may also attach a persona-scoped `memory` MCP server so its knowledge-graph tools operate on that persona file, and/or a ChromaDB-backed store (`src/utils/chromadb.lisp`, a REST binding for ChromaDB v2) used by `src/prompts/prompt-decoration.lisp` for memory/diary retrieval and by tool execution for knowledge-graph sync. Persona config may also enable built-in filesystem tools with `:enable-filesystem-tools t`, built-in web grounding tools with `:enable-web-tools t` (`webSearch` via `GOOGLE:web-search` and `hyperspecSearch` via `GOOGLE:hyperspec-search`), the built-in `eval` tool with `:enable-eval t`, and prompt timestamping with `:include-timestamp t` / prompt model labels with `:include-model t`. The eval tool requires per-request user approval for the exact submitted expression and returns captured values/stdout/stderr. Timestamp and model prefixes are transient request-time prompt decoration, not stored conversation history. `chat` also accepts transient per-turn `:files` attachments plus a convenience `:file` alias for one pathname: files, directories, and wildcards are expanded into a deduplicated file list, Gemini/Google receive MIME blobs when possible, OpenAI-compatible requests fall back to text parts (or image data URLs for images), and the attachments are not saved in `conversation-messages`. The persona root is always allowed, and additional approved directories are persisted in a separate persona-owned `filesystem-allowlist.lisp` file.

## Key conventions

- Every source file lives in `(in-package "CHATBOT")`.
- `src/core/package.lisp` shadowing-imports `DEFUN`, `FUNCALL`, `LET*`, `MULTIPLE-VALUE-BIND` from `SERIES`, `LET`/`NAMED-LAMBDA` from `NAMED-LET`, and `COMPOSE` from `FUNCTION`. Inside this package, do not assume you are using the plain `CL` variants of those names.
- When seeding or inspecting stored conversation history, assistant-side preload messages should use the `"model"` role. The backend adapters normalize roles for OpenAI and Google when building requests.
- Route outbound HTTP calls through `post-web-request`/`get-web-request`/`patch-web-request`/`delete-web-request` in `src/utils/http-utils.lisp` so logging, secret redaction, and timeout defaults stay consistent; timeouts (`15s` connect, `120s` read) and the underlying HTTP functions are resolved from the active `runtime-context`, not hardcoded, so tests can substitute fakes.
- MCP tool exposure is backend-specific. Reuse the existing translation helpers in `src/mcp/mcp.lisp` plus the schema/payload helpers in `src/utils/json-utils.lisp` / `src/payloads/payloads.lisp` (`translate-mcp-tool-to-openai`, `translate-mcp-tool-to-gemini-fn`, `gemini-tool-parameters`, `make-interaction-payload`) instead of hand-building tool payloads in new code.
- Prefer explicit `defclass`/`defstruct` component types over ad-hoc plists/`assoc` for new core data (see the "God Object" and "Data Structures" resolutions/notes in `TECHNICAL_DEBT.md`); this is an active, enforced direction, not just aspirational.
- Threads, subprocesses, and other cleanup-sensitive resources should be registered with a `resource-supervisor` (`register-supervised-thread`/`register-supervised-process` in `src/core/data.lisp`) so `with-resource-supervisor`/context shutdown can guarantee teardown instead of relying on manual cleanup.
- `FUNCTIONAL_REFACTOR.md` describes the long-term direction (immutability/copy-on-write, pure core + imperative shell, explicit effect descriptions) — treat it as intent/vision, not a description of current code. `TECHNICAL_DEBT.md` tracks current prioritized debt (P0/P1/P2) and recently-resolved items; check it before large refactors so you don't duplicate in-flight work or reintroduce retired patterns.
